mainTopic: Measuring a field with crevices and boulders (in הקדש, in a sale, and in a קידושין condition), and רבי מאיר's rule of the doubled condition (תנאי כפול)
overview: The גמרא quotes a משנה: someone who is מקדיש his field while the יובל is in force redeems it at fifty shekels for each area sown with a חומר of barley. Crevices ten טפחים deep or boulders ten טפחים high are not measured with the field. The גמרא asks why these spots are not redeemed on their own, since a ברייתא shows that even tiny areas count as a 'field.' מר עוקבא בר חמא answers that the crevices are full of water and cannot be planted, and smaller dips and bumps are just normal parts of a field. In a sale, though, big crevices are left out even when dry, because, as רב פפא explains, a buyer wants one connected field. The גמרא decides that a קידושין condition about owning a בית כור follows the הקדש rule, because the husband can say he will take the trouble to farm those spots. Then a new משנה opens: רבי מאיר says every condition must be doubled, stating both outcomes like the condition with בני גד and בני ראובן. רבי חנינא בן גמליאל answers that the 'if not' half of that פסוק had its own purpose. The גמרא begins showing how רבי מאיר defends his proof from the extra words 'in the land of Canaan,' and this continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The fixed price for redeeming a consecrated field, and what is left out of the measurement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה. A consecrated field is redeemed at fifty shekels per בית כור. Crevices or boulders that are ten טפחים deep or high are not measured with the field. Smaller ones are measured with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone consecrates his field while the יובל is in force, he pays fifty silver shekels for every area that is sown with a חומר of barley. If the field has crevices ten handbreadths deep or boulders ten handbreadths high, they are not measured with it. If they are smaller than that, they are measured with it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a משנה that sets the redemption price for a consecrated field. It then explains which parts of the land are left out when the field is measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה fixes the price by area, not by how good the land is: fifty shekels for each area sown with a חומר of barley. A dip or rise of ten טפחים makes that spot count as a separate area, so it is not measured with the field. Anything smaller is just part of the field.

keyTerms.meaning: One who consecrates (dedicates property to the בית המקדש)
The fiftieth (Jubilee) year; its laws control how a consecrated field is redeemed
A large dry measure, equal to a כור
Crevices or deep dips in the ground
Boulders or rocky rises
Handbreadths; ten טפחים is the common size for a separate area

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the base text for the whole discussion. The question in the next steps comes from its rule that crevices and boulders are 'not measured with it.'

phrases.english: One who consecrates his field at a time when the Jubilee is in force,
gives, for an area sown with a חומר of barley,
fifty silver shekels.
If there were crevices ten handbreadths deep
or boulders ten handbreadths high,
they are not measured with it.
phrases.notes: "It" is the field. These spots are not counted when working out how much he must pay.

phrases.english: Less than this, they are measured with it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the discussion by quoting the base text.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A consecrated field is redeemed at fifty shekels per בית כור. Crevices or boulders of ten טפחים are not measured with the field; smaller ones are.

steps.title: Why aren't the crevices and boulders consecrated on their own?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא accepts that the crevices and boulders are not part of the main field. It asks why they shouldn't still be consecrated and redeemed as their own separate areas.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we discussed this: Fine, they are not consecrated together with the land. But let them be consecrated on their own!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. If these spots are separate from the field, why aren't they redeemed separately at the תורה's price?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only said these spots are 'not measured with it.' The גמרא points out that being separate should not make them free of הקדש. They should be measured and paid for as their own little fields.

keyTerms.meaning: And we discussed it; introduces an earlier difficulty with the text
Granted; fine
On their own; by themselves

phrases.english: And we discussed it:
Granted that they are not consecrated together with the land,
let them be consecrated on their own!
phrases.notes: In other words, they should need their own payment, at the same rate of fifty shekels per בית כור.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the rule just quoted from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that deep crevices and high boulders are simply 'not measured with' the field
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Being separate from the field should not free these spots from הקדש. They should be redeemed on their own.

steps.title: A suggested answer: areas smaller than a בית כור don't count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests an answer: maybe a spot smaller than a full בית כור is too small to matter, so it is not redeemed on its own. This answer is about to be tested.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: as long as it is not a full בית כור, it is not significant.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to its question. It is setting up the next move, where this answer will be checked against a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the תורה's price is stated for a full בית כור, so tiny spots like crevices would not count as a field at all. If that were true, the crevices would have no redemption price.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say; introduces a possible answer
An area that takes a כור of seed to plant
Significant; counts

phrases.english: And if you will say:

phrases.aramaic: כַּמָּה דְּלָא הָוֵי בֵּית כּוֹר לָא חֲשִׁיב,
phrases.english: as long as it is not a בית כור, it is not significant,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question in step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crevices should be redeemed on their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: Spots smaller than a בית כור don't count, so they have no redemption price (this answer is rejected in the next step).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that even tiny areas count as a field
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer using a ברייתא. The word 'שדה' teaches that even very small areas, down to a רובע, are redeemed at the תורה's price.
steps.simpleTranslation: But contrast this with a ברייתא: Why does the verse say 'a field'? Since it says 'the sowing of a חומר of barley at fifty,' I would only know about someone who consecrated that much. How do we include a לתך, half a לתך, a סאה, a תרקב, half a תרקב, and even a רובע? The verse says 'field,' meaning any size!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 3. It quotes a ברייתא showing that the תורה's price applies even to tiny pieces of land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא learns from the extra word 'שדה' that any size of field is redeemed at the same rate. So the size of the crevices cannot be the reason they are left out. The question from step 2 comes back.

keyTerms.meaning: And contrast them; introduces a source that seems to contradict
The verse says; points to a word in the פסוק that teaches something
To include
Half a כור
Half a סאה
A quarter of a קב, a very small measure

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא does not argue with the משנה. It only proves that small size is not a good reason, so the גמרא needs a different explanation for the crevices.

phrases.english: But contrast it with this:
"A field": why does the verse say this?
Since it says:
"the sowing of a חומר of barley at fifty,"

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לִי אֶלָּא שֶׁהִקְדִּישׁ בָּעִנְיָן הַזֶּה,
phrases.english: I only know about one who consecrated in this way,
phrases.notes: He means a full area for sowing a חומר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested answer in step 3, which brings back the question from step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Fully rejects the idea that spots smaller than a בית כור don't count
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא teaches from 'שדה' that even a רובע-sized area is redeemed at the תורה's price.

steps.title: מר עוקבא בר חמא: the crevices are full of water
steps.stepSummary: מר עוקבא בר חמא explains that the משנה is talking about crevices full of water. Land that cannot be planted is not a 'field,' so it is not redeemed at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר עוקבא בר חמא said: Here we are dealing with crevices full of water, because they cannot be planted.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives the real answer to the question. These crevices are not redeemed on their own because they are not plantable land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is not size, which the ברייתא ruled out. It is the kind of land. The תורה's price is per area of sowing, so a spot that cannot be sown at all is not part of the 'field' price.

keyTerms.meaning: Here we are dealing with; narrows the case
Full of water
Fit for sowing

steps.whatToRemember: Size doesn't matter: even a tiny field is redeemed. What matters is whether the land can be planted. Water-filled crevices and high boulders can't be, so they are left out.

phrases.english: Mar Ukva bar Chama said:
Here we are dealing with crevices full of water,
because they are not fit for sowing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא בַּר חָמָא: הָכָא בִּנְקָעִים מְלֵאִים מַיִם עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from step 2, which came back after step 4.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The crevices are ordinary land and should be redeemed on their own.
steps.terutzMaskana: The crevices are full of water and cannot be planted, so they are not a 'field' and have no redemption price.

steps.title: The wording of the משנה supports the answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the משנה's wording fits מר עוקבא's answer. The crevices are listed together with high boulders, which also can't be planted. The גמרא accepts the proof.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches the crevices alongside high boulders. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up מר עוקבא's answer from the way the משנה is written. Then it accepts the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Boulders clearly can't be sown. Since the משנה lists crevices together with them, the crevices must also be land that can't be sown, like crevices full of water.

keyTerms.meaning: It is also precise; the wording supports this
Similar to; alongside
Learn from it; the point is accepted

phrases.english: It is also precise,
phrases.notes: The words of the משנה themselves hint at this answer.

phrases.english: since it teaches them alongside high boulders,
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי, דְּקָתָנֵי דּוּמְיָא דִסְלָעִים גְּבוֹהִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 5 from the wording of the משנה in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: מר עוקבא בר חמא's explanation that the crevices are full of water and can't be planted
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה puts crevices side by side with high boulders, which also can't be planted.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The crevices in the משנה are unplantable (full of water), so like the boulders they are left out of the field and are not redeemed on their own.

steps.title: Then Shallow Crevices Should Not Count Either
steps.stepSummary: If unplantable spots don't count as 'field,' then even crevices and boulders smaller than ten טפחים should be left out too.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then even spots less than ten טפחים should also not be counted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges מר עוקבא's reason. If 'can't be planted' is what makes a spot not a field, why does the משנה count smaller crevices and boulders?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 5 said a spot that can't be planted is not a 'field.' But a shallow water-filled crevice or a low boulder can't be planted either. So the ten-טפחים line seems to have no basis.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your reasoning is correct
Less than this (here, less than ten טפחים)
Also, too

phrases.english: If so,
even less than this, also!
phrases.notes: 'Less than this' means crevices or boulders smaller than ten טפחים, which the משנה does count.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, אֲפִילּוּ פָּחוֹת מִיכֵּן נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'unplantable means not a field' reasoning that was just accepted in steps 5-6.
steps.kashyaTarget: מר עוקבא בר חמא's reason that unplantable land is not a 'field.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Small water-filled crevices and low boulders are also unplantable, so the reason should exclude them too, yet the משנה counts them.

steps.title: Small Dips and Bumps Are Normal Parts of a Field
steps.stepSummary: Spots under ten טפחים are called the 'cracks' and 'spine' of the ground. They are ordinary features of every field.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those are called the cracks of the ground; they are called the spine of the ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that small crevices and low boulders are simply part of what a normal field looks like, so they are counted with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big crevice or boulder (ten טפחים or more) is its own separate spot. Small dips and bumps are expected in any field, so they are treated as the field itself, even if they can't be planted.

keyTerms.meaning: The cracks or hollows of the ground: small dips
The spine of the ground: small raised ridges or bumps
They are called

phrases.english: Those are called the cracks of the ground,
they are called the spine of the ground.
phrases.notes: This refers to the low boulders, like bumps along a backbone.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ נְאגָנֵי דְאַרְעָא מִיקְּרוּ, שִׁדְרָא דְאַרְעָא מִקְּרוּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefinition: small features are part of the field's normal shape, not separate spots.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any unplantable spot, big or small, should be left out of the field.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only big spots (ten טפחים or more) stand apart. Smaller ones are normal parts of a field and are counted.

steps.title: The Rule for Crevices When Selling a Field
steps.stepSummary: A parallel משנה about selling a בית כור says big crevices and boulders are not measured with the field. מר עוקבא בר חמא adds that this is true even when the crevices are dry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Regarding a sale we learned: If someone tells another, 'I am selling you a בית כור of earth,' and there were crevices ten טפחים deep or boulders ten טפחים high, they are not measured with it. If less, they are measured with it. And מר עוקבא בר חמא said: even if they are not full of water.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source about selling land, which sets up a comparison with the הקדש case. Here מר עוקבא rules more strictly than he did for הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הקדש, מר עוקבא said only water-filled crevices are left out (step 5). For a sale, he says big crevices are left out even when dry and plantable. This contrast sets up the questions that follow.

keyTerms.meaning: Regarding a sale
We learned (in a משנה)
They are measured together with it (counted as part of the field)

keyTerms.term: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְלֵאִים מַיִם
keyTerms.meaning: Even though they are not full of water

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up מר עוקבא's two rulings. For הקדש, only water-filled crevices are left out. For a sale, big crevices are left out even when dry.

phrases.english: Regarding a sale, we learned:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in בבא בתרא 102b.

phrases.english: One who says to his fellow:
"I am selling you a בית כור of earth,"

phrases.aramaic: וְהָיוּ שָׁם נְקָעִים עֲמוּקִּים עֲשָׂרָה טְפָחִים
phrases.english: and there were crevices there ten handbreadths deep
or boulders ten handbreadths high,
they are not measured with it.
Less than this, they are measured with it.

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין מְלֵאִים מַיִם.
phrases.english: even though they are not full of water.
phrases.notes: Compare step 5, where he said the הקדש rule applies only to crevices full of water.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel case (sale) to contrast with the הקדש case just settled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In a sale, crevices ten טפחים deep or boulders ten טפחים high are not counted in the measurement, even if the crevices are dry.

steps.title: Why Is a Sale Different?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, for a sale, even dry crevices are left out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind מר עוקבא's stricter sale rule. This sets up רב פפא's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For הקדש, a dry crevice still counts because it can be planted. So why should a dry crevice not count in a sale? The גמרא wants the reason for the difference.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the ruling just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason a sale leaves out even dry big crevices, unlike הקדש.

steps.title: A Buyer Wants One Smooth Field
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that a buyer doesn't want to pay for one field and end up with something that looks like two or three separate pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Because a person doesn't want to pay his money for one field and have it look to him like two or three places.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives the reason: in a sale, what the buyer wants matters, and he wants one connected field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A big crevice or boulder cuts the field into pieces, even if the crevice is dry and plantable. Since the buyer paid for one whole field, those areas are not counted toward what he bought.

keyTerms.meaning: His money
And it will look to him
Places, separate spots

steps.whyThisMatters: The sale rule is based on what the buyer expects, not on whether the land can be planted. That is why it can differ from הקדש.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Because a person does not want
to give his money for one field
and have it look to him like two or three places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין אָדָם רוֹצֶה
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In a sale, the buyer's wish for one connected field is what counts, so big crevices are left out even when dry.

steps.title: Is Our Case Like הקדש or Like a Sale?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which model applies to the קידושין case: הקדש, where dry crevices count, or a sale, where they don't.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here, what? Do we compare it to הקדש, or do we compare it to a sale?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns back to its own case, a man who betroths a woman on condition that he owns a בית כור of land. It asks which of the two rules fits.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the man's land is a full בית כור only if you count big dry crevices. Under the הקדש rule he owns a בית כור and the קידושין works. Under the sale rule he does not, and the condition fails.

keyTerms.meaning: Here, what is the law?
We compare it
Consecrated property

phrases.english: Here, what?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means our case: a man who betroths a woman on condition that he owns a בית כור of land.

phrases.english: Do we compare it to consecration,
or do we compare it to a sale?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכָא מַאי? לְהֶקְדֵּשׁ מְדַמֵּינַן לַהּ, אוֹ לְמֶכֶר מְדַמֵּינַן לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two models just laid out (הקדש and sale) to ask about the קידושין case.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether big dry crevices count toward the בית כור in a קידושין condition.

steps.title: It Is Like הקדש: The Husband Will Do the Extra Work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that our case is like הקדש. The husband can tell the woman he will take the trouble to plant those spots and bring in the produce.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that we compare it to הקדש, because he can say to her: I will go to the trouble, plant, and bring in the produce.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the dry crevices count, just as in הקדש, so the man does own a בית כור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason for the sale rule doesn't apply here. The woman wasn't buying a smooth field. She only needs him to own a בית כור of usable land. Since he is willing to make the extra effort to farm the uneven spots, the land counts.

keyTerms.meaning: It stands to reason, it makes sense
I take the trouble, make the effort
And I bring (the produce)

steps.whatToRemember: There are three cases. In הקדש, dry crevices count. In a sale, big crevices never count, because a buyer wants one connected field. In a קידושין condition, the rule follows הקדש, because the husband can say he will put in the effort to farm those spots.

phrases.english: It stands to reason that we compare it to consecration,
because he says to her:
phrases.notes: 'Her' is the woman he betrothed on this condition.

phrases.english: I will take the trouble, and sow, and bring.
phrases.notes: He means he'll plant even the low and high spots and bring the crops up from there.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The קידושין case follows הקדש: big dry crevices count toward the בית כור.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In a קידושין condition about owning a בית כור, the land is measured as in הקדש, because the husband's willingness to do extra work makes those spots count.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: A condition must be doubled like the one with בני גד and בני ראובן
steps.stepSummary: The new משנה opens with רבי מאיר's rule that a condition only works if it is stated like the condition with בני גד and בני ראובן, where both outcomes were spelled out.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר says: Any condition that is not like the condition of בני גד and בני ראובן is not a condition. The proof is that the תורה states both sides: 'If they pass over' and also 'If they will not pass over armed.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts, and רבי מאיר gives a rule about how to set up a valid condition. He brings proof from the deal משה made with the tribes of גד and ראובן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה told the tribes what would happen if they kept the condition, and also what would happen if they did not. רבי מאיר learns from this that every condition must spell out both sides. If it does not, the condition does not count, and the deal goes ahead as if no condition had been made.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין, 'our משנה'. It marks the start of a new משנה.
A condition attached to a deal or a קידושין.
The tribes of גד and ראובן, who asked to settle east of the ירדן.
'As it is said.' This introduces a פסוק as proof.
'And it is written.' This brings a second פסוק.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: a condition must state both the 'if yes' outcome and the 'if no' outcome (a תנאי כפול), like the condition with בני גד and בני ראובן.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Not a condition' does not cancel the deal. It means the condition is ignored and the deal stands without it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the main source for the rule of תנאי כפול, the 'doubled condition', which comes up across all of הלכה on conditions.

phrases.english: MISHNA: Rabbi Meir says:
Any condition that is not
like the condition of the children of Gad and the children of Reuben,
phrases.notes: He means a condition that spells out both sides: what happens if it is kept, and what happens if it is not.

phrases.english: is not a condition.
As it is said: "And he said to them,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יַעַבְרוּ בְנֵי גָד וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן״.
phrases.english: if the children of Gad and the children of Reuben pass over."
And it is written: "But if they will not pass over armed."

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ רַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹמֵר: כׇּל תְּנַאי שֶׁאֵינוֹ כִּתְנַאי בְּנֵי גָּד וּבְנֵי רְאוּבֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, moving away from the field-measuring discussion in steps 9-13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A condition that does not state both the positive and the negative outcome, the way the condition with בני גד and בני ראובן did, is not a valid condition.

steps.title: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל: That double wording was needed for its own reason
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל argues that the 'if not' half of that פסוק had a special purpose, so it cannot serve as a source for a general rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל says: The תורה had to say the 'if not' part. Otherwise, you might have thought that if they did not cross over, they would not inherit even in ארץ כנען.
steps.whatsHappening: Within the same משנה, a second תנא pushes back on רבי מאיר's proof from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'if not' half was needed to tell us something specific: even if the tribes failed the condition, they still keep a share in ארץ כנען. Since that half has its own job, it does not prove that every condition needs both sides. So רבי מאיר's source falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The matter needed to be said.' It had its own purpose.
'If not for this,' or 'otherwise.'
'It would be implied,' or 'you might have understood.'
'They will inherit,' meaning they receive a portion of land.

phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel says:
It was necessary to state the matter,
phrases.notes: He is talking about the second half of the פסוק, the 'if they will not pass over' part.

phrases.english: for if not so,
it would have been implied
that even in the land of Canaan they would not inherit.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר: צָרִיךְ הַדָּבָר לְאוֹמְרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי מאיר's proof by giving the 'if not' half of the פסוק a different job.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof from the פסוק that every condition must be doubled.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The 'if not' clause was needed to teach that the tribes still inherit in ארץ כנען, so it does not teach a general rule about conditions.

steps.title: The גמרא admits רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's point is strong
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by saying רבי חנינא בן גמליאל made a good argument against רבי מאיר. This sets up the question of how רבי מאיר could answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: רבי חנינא בן גמליאל spoke well to רבי מאיר!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says that רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's objection seems to knock out רבי מאיר's proof. This is a setup: the next step will show how רבי מאיר could respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'he spoke well' is a way of raising a challenge: if the objection is so good, how does רבי מאיר keep his rule? Nothing is resolved yet. The גמרא is only pointing out the pressure on רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גְּמָרָא. It marks where the discussion of the משנה begins.
'He is saying well,' meaning a strong and reasonable argument.

phrases.english: GEMARA: He is speaking well to him,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר!
phrases.english: Rabbi Ḥanina ben Gamliel, to Rabbi Meir!
phrases.notes: There is an unspoken question here: so how would רבי מאיר answer?

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְרַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The גמרא accepts that the objection in step 15 is strong and turns it into a challenge against רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's proof from the פסוק of בני גד and בני ראובן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the 'if not' clause is needed to teach that they still inherit in ארץ כנען, then רבי מאיר has no source for the doubled-condition rule.

steps.title: רבי מאיר's reply: The פסוק has extra words
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר would answer that to teach only what רבי חנינא בן גמליאל said, the פסוק could have stopped at 'they shall receive a possession among you.' Instead it adds 'in the land of Canaan,' which hints at a further lesson.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר could tell you: If you think this פסוק does not come to teach a doubled condition, it should just say 'But if they will not pass over, they shall receive a possession among you.' Yet it says 'in the land of Canaan.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts giving רבי מאיר's defense. He points to wording in the פסוק that seems more than needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'They shall receive a possession among you' would already teach רבי חנינא בן גמליאל's point, that they still get land. Because the פסוק adds 'in the land of Canaan,' the extra words must be there for something else. רבי מאיר says that something is the doubled-condition rule; the explanation of how these words teach it continues on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He could say to you.' This introduces how a תנא would answer.
'If it enters your mind,' meaning if you were to think.
A 'doubled condition' that states both the positive and the negative outcome.
'Let it write,' meaning the פסוק should have said only this.

steps.confusionAlert: The step ends with just the words 'in the land of Canaan.' The point is that these words look extra, and the גמרא goes on to explain them right after this.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir could say to you:
If it enters your mind
that it does not come to teach a doubled condition,
let it write: "But if they will not pass over
they shall receive a possession among you,"
[why does it add] "in the land of Canaan"?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִי סָלְקָא דַעְתָּךְ לָאו לִתְנַאי כָּפוּל הוּא דַּאֲתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 16 by pointing to extra words in the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording in the פסוק (a ייתור לשון) shows the פסוק must be teaching the doubled-condition rule.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The 'if not' clause was written only to teach that the tribes keep their share in ארץ כנען, so it gives no general rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'They shall receive a possession among you' would have taught that point by itself. The added words 'in the land of Canaan' point to the doubled-condition rule, and the full explanation continues in the גמרא.
